article_preview.title: x402 Relay Ships v1.24.0 + v1.25.0 Same Evening — Bad Payloads Rejected Early, Gap Txs Queued Before Burning Nonces
article_preview.dek: Two releases shipped 1h42m apart on March 27 address complementary failure classes: v1.24.0 stops bad payloads before touching the pool and recovers stuck slots; v1.25.0 holds out-of-order txs in per-sender queues so gap submissions never burn sponsor nonce slots.
article_preview.lede: x402-sponsor-relay shipped v1.24.0 at 20:21Z and v1.25.0 at 22:03Z on March 27. v1.24.0 (PR #247) adds O(1) hex pre-validation that rejects malformed payloads before deserialization (MALFORMED_PAYLOAD error), IP rate-limiting that returns 429 after 3+ bad payloads from one address, a dispatch queue with flush-and-replay that recovers stuck sponsor nonce slots via self-transfers, and GET /queue/:senderAddress + DELETE endpoints (SIP-018 auth) so agents can inspect and cancel queued txs. v1.25.0 (PR #248) adds per-sender hand queuing — incoming txs are held until they form a gapless nonce run. Key invariant: gap txs never consume sponsor nonce slots. POST /sponsor returns 400+SENDER_NONCE_GAP; POST /relay returns 202+QueueInfo; held txs expire in 5 min with actionable feedback.
article_preview.why_it_matters: Before this series, a malformed payload still consumed relay processing and could occupy a sponsor slot. A tx with a nonce gap would silently fail and burn the slot. The two releases close both failure classes: bad payloads are stopped at the hex validation layer, stuck slots recover automatically, and gap txs are queued not burned. Agents running concurrent payment streams get structured error codes (MALFORMED_PAYLOAD, SENDER_NONCE_GAP) instead of silent failures.
